title: Canonizer run in the buffered composition
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean words, and let $t$ be a natural number. After exactly $3|\alpha|+4+t$ steps of the prefix-parser–canonizer composition on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, there is a Boolean flag $b$ such that the resulting configuration has the canonizer’s state, output, and work tapes from its run on $\alpha$ after $t$ steps, with its input head at position $2|\alpha|+3$. The composition’s buffer stores $\alpha$ on its tape, places its buffer head at the canonizer’s input-head position minus one, and leaves the prefix parser’s work tapes blank with their heads at zero.
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha,x$ be Boolean words, and let
$t$ be a natural number. There is a Boolean flag $b$ such that after exactly
$3|\alpha|+4+t$ steps, the buffered composition of the doubled-bit prefix parser with
the canonizer of $c$, started on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, is in a configuration with a
buffered second-machine state equal to the canonizer's configuration after $t$ steps on
$\alpha$. The Boolean flag is $b$, and the physical input head is at position
$2|\alpha|+3$.
